definition_used: When a journal/publisher/institution states that one or more authors have not met the journal/publisher/institution’s standards of publishing and/or research ethics. RW will use this reason when no other information about the correction/EOC/retraction is available (i.e., the notice only states that there was an ethical violation), or when the ethical violation (as an additional reason) cannot be addressed by existing reasons.
caution: The definition is broad and often used as a catch-all when specifics are unavailable. The assignment of manuscript categories is based on the general notion of ethical standards, which can encompass authorship integrity and editorial governance, but without further detail, the mapping is inferential.
semantic_rationale: The reason indicates a failure to meet publishing/research ethics standards by authors, as stated by a journal/publisher/institution. This broadly implicates authorship and disclosure integrity (attribution_authorship_disclosure_integrity) and the editorial/peer review governance that enforces such standards (editorial_peer_review_governance). The problem object is the article as a whole, and the process involves investigation and policy enforcement by the journal/publisher or institution.
